decision_rule: Per instance, rank {harden-quarter (tau0=0.25), harden-tau05, harden-tau075, harden (tau0=1)} by best-of-16 at 1e-4. PRIMARY (descriptive/localizing): report the smallest tau0 within 1e-3 of the instance best and the tau0 where performance degrades >1e-3; the break point localizes where the full morph goes wrong. SECONDARY: trajectory analysis from replays — compare the morph-phase paths of tau0=0.25 (good) vs tau0=1 (bad): does the full morph destroy a good disk-phase arrangement, or never find one? No confirmatory claim; this is anomaly localization.
hypothesis: The C05 anomaly (cross n=5: full harden 6.6569 vs quarter/half/nocompress/rigid all 6.3246) is a morph-path pathology: starting from full disks, the long morph pulls crosses into a worse basin that the shorter morph avoids. A tau0 sweep localizes the breaking point. Understanding where hardening HURTS bounds where it can help.
question: Where in the morph path does full hardening break on cross (and why)?
title: Tau0 sweep localizing the cross morph pathology
